newsitem.title: FRANCE: Israeli-Palestinian parliamentarians on joint tour.
newsitem.headline: Israeli-Palestinian parliamentarians on joint tour.

text.p: Israeli and Palestinian parliamentarians, speaking at the end of an unprecedented joint European tour, pledged on Tuesday to work to build momentum towards Middle East peace.

"Our joint wish is to send a strong message to our respective societies saying mutual recognition is at work. We intend to transform our action into a people-to-people movement essential for peace to grow and flourish," said Israel's Yehuda Lancry of the ruling Likud party's Gesher wing.
"For both people, there is no other path than the choice of peace," echoed Palestinian Marwan Bargouti, secretary-general of President Yasser Arafat's Fatah movement.
The two were among a dozen parliamentarians from each side who jointly toured Spain and France in the past week at the invitation of the European Union (EU).
Three parliamentarians from each side addressed the news conference at the French National Assembly. Among the Israelis was Maxim Levy, brother of Foreign Minister David Levy.
Both sides paid tribute to the 15-nation EU which Lancry said was an excellent model for co-existence and development.
The parliamentarians said they communicated during the tour in Arabic, mother tongue for the Palestinians and those Israelis born in Arab countries, as well as in English.
Some Palestinians also spoke fluent Hebrew, especially Quadura Fares who learned the language during a 14-year-stint in Israeli prisons for guerrilla activity.

Bargouti however made clear the Palestinians had no intention of giving rubber stamp approval to Israeli government policies and said the dialogue's ultimate result would have to be an independent Palestinian state with rapid progress before on other demands.
He warned of a possible explosion of new violence if Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu persisted in creating a new Jewish neighbourhood between Jerusalem and Bethlehem.

Knesset (parliament) deputy speaker David Tal of the religious Shas party put his arm around Bargouti's shoulder and said: "I want to ask my friend Marwan, please don't make threats, they can only make the situation regress."

Bargouti said he found much in common with Tal, who is of Tunisian origin, "and generally with all those Knesset members born in Arab countries who understand Arabs better and are more open to peace."

Morocco-born Lancry rejoined that while there was a centuries-old common Arabic culture between some Israelis and the Palestinians, "the Israeli pioneer in peace-making was, after all, the Polish-born (late premier) Menachem Begin."
Another historical note was provided by the presence as assistant to the delegation of Palestinian Nadia Sartawi.

Her father, Issam Sartawi, was a Palestinian pioneer in ties with Israelis. He was assassinated over a decade ago by gunmen of the hardline Abu Nidal faction while representing the Palestine Liberation Organisation at a meeting of the Socialist International in Portugal.
